page: Microsoft Azure E64as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data highlights strong computational and memory performance. The single-core CPU performance under stress-ng and the PassMark CPU score both rank in the top 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is robust, with uncached large-block read speeds reaching 203.18 GB/sec and write speeds at 131.02 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also achieve top-tier performance. For database workloads, PassMark database operations rank in the top 10%, and Redis SET operations reach 98.7 million operations per second.

This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale database operations, in-memory caching, and data analytics. It also demonstrates strong capabilities for small to medium-scale language model inference, achieving top-tier token generation speeds for 135M and 7B parameter models, though performance drops to average levels for larger 70B models. The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on external network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider for I/O-heavy applications.
